title: Clocking on
story: Your first night shift at the pizzeria starts now. Before the first order comes in, the shop's computer needs a start-of-shift script that announces the shift, works out how many slices are ready, and warns the driver about the oven.

requirements.text: The first line it prints is exactly `Shift started`.
It prints how many slices are ready: 6 pizzas with 8 slices each. Luau must do the multiplication, so don't work it out yourself.
It uses `warn` at least once, with any message about the oven.
It has at least one comment explaining something.

hints: Each requirement is one line of code. Write them in the order the story describes.
Text goes in quotes. A sum goes without quotes, so Luau works it out before printing.
A comment starts with two dashes. Put one above a line saying why it's there.

static.fail: Create a Script (not a LocalScript or ModuleScript) named `Hello` inside the `Test01` folder.
Let Luau do the multiplication: put the sum itself in the print, like a number, a star, and a number.

check:
local path = "ServerScriptService.Course.Test01.Hello"
local run = Course.run(path)
Course.check("r2", run.ok, "Your script stopped with an error: " .. tostring(run.error))
local first = run.prints[1]
Course.check("r3", first == "Shift started", "The first printed line should be exactly `Shift started`, but it was " .. Course.show(first) .. ". Check the spelling, capitals and spaces.")
local found48 = false
for _, line in run.prints do
	if string.find(line, "%f[%d]48%f[%D]") then
		found48 = true
	end
end
Course.check("r4", found48, "None of the printed lines contained the number of slices. Your script printed " .. Course.show(run.prints) .. ".")
Course.check("r5", #run.warns >= 1, "Your script didn't warn anything. Use `warn` for the oven message, not `print`.")
local source = Course.source(path) or ""
Course.check("r6", string.find(source, "%-%-") ~= nil, "Add at least one comment, starting with two dashes.")
steps: Line 1: print exactly `Shift started` (a capital S, then a lowercase s in started).
Print how many slices are ready: 6 pizzas with 8 slices each. Write the sum itself in the print, using `*` to multiply (Luau doesn't understand `x`), so Luau works out 48 for you.
Use `warn` (not `print`) for any message about the oven, like `Oven is hot`.
Add at least one comment: a line starting with `--` that explains something.
example:
Shift started
48
Oven is hot   (this line shows in orange, because it's a warn)
